newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares mixed at open, second liners up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares mixed at open, second liners up.

text.p: Singapore shares were mixed in morning trading on Thursday with investors focusing on second liners as activity in blue chips dwindled.
"A lot of interest is in second board and Malaysian stocks," said one institutional dealer who saw little movement in blue chips throughout the day.

Malaysian motor group, Tan Chong Motor, surged on the reopening of trade in its stock which had been suspended since November 22. At 0312 GMT, 14.16 million shares had been traded, and it was up Singapore $0.07 to S$2.72, following news that the company was restructuring into four component businesses.

"Malaysian shares are definitely worthwhile, they are the most active and most intersting at the moment," a dealer said. Singapore's over-the-counter UOB-OTC Index was up 2.03 at 1,229.61 at 0312 GMT.
However, Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was down 11.10 points to 2,209.26.

Total market volume was 52.46 million shares, producing 112 losers to 89 gainers. DBS foreign, Sing Press foreign and Elec & Eltek were higer while Cerebos Pacific, OUB foreign and Cycle & Carriage were lower.
